handoff: Design (a) implemented as asked: intake writes spec.md, storyFile and the GR6 base record read spec.md and fall back to story.md, nothing is renamed; PRD/README/bundled assets updated; tests at store/decide/record seams. Suite 1204 pass, typecheck clean. Non-blocking: repo-local workflows and triage skill still say story.md (follow-up after the release).

findings.title: Repo-local triage skill and workflows still say story.md
findings.detail:
The spec's Where lists `.agents/norn/workflows/*.yaml` and `.agents/skills/triage/SKILL.md` as repo-local mentions. They still say story.md (triage.yaml:17-31, spec.yaml, fix.yaml:17, quick.yaml:17,44, story.yaml:20-48, triage SKILL.md:3,12,26,65). Once a release with this change runs here, intake writes spec.md, and the triage step would then be told to write `## Triage` into a story.md that does not exist. The handoff defers this on purpose: the released norn still writes story.md, and .agents/norn/ is off limits to agents. The release skill, however, was moved to the dual-name wording ('spec.md, or story.md in a story intaken before the rename'), which is safe under both releases. The triage skill could have taken the same wording now.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: File a follow-up issue to switch the repo-local workflows and the triage skill to spec.md, or to the dual-name wording, right after this ships.

findings.title: Corrupt inbox item id says spec.md even for a legacy story.md
findings.detail:
The id `corrupt:<story>:spec.md` is fixed, while the title names the real file (story.md in a legacy folder). An inbox-history entry keyed on the old id `corrupt:<story>:story.md` will not match after an upgrade. That is harmless; the item simply reappears once.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: None needed, or use a name-neutral id such as `corrupt:<story>:spec`.
